summary: Niharranjan Ray was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1924-1926) and Leiden University (~1935-1936), later working at the University of Calcutta (~1936-1965) and directing the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1965-1970).

Nika Jovic works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007-2008) and earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Alexander von Rospatt and earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and Jens-Uwe Hartmann (attested 2013), later working at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nina Mirnig is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2010, founded the University of Oxford in 2008, and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020).

Ninian Smart specialized in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at The Glasgow Academy, The Queen's College, Oxford (~1948-1954), and Yale (~1950-1952), he held posts at Nottingham, Birmingham, Lancaster (1967), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 1993-2001).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyupane, and completed his doctorate under Peter Bisschop at Leiden University in 2015. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019) and Leiden University (2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD ~1924-1926). He lectured at Calcutta University (1917) before serving in the Archaeological Survey of India (1929-1950), becoming Director General of Archaeology in India (1948-1950).

Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency University (~1929-1933) and the University of Calcutta (~1931-1935), later serving at Krishnath College (~1938-1942), the National Archives of India (~1942-1958), and Calcutta University (~1970-1975).
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under Richard Gombrich by 2003. She was also a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1954-1961), he held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1964-1974), the University of Tokyo (~1974-1994), Taisho University (~1994-2004), and the Open University of Japan (~1994-1998).
Noboru Ueda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, Hajime Sakurabe, and Ichijo Ogawa, later serving at Otani University Junior College and as professor at Otani University (~1988-2015).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University (attested 1962) under Yutaka Ochihara. He held assistant professor posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1988-1998), where he served as a Research Fellow (~1998-2001), and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2004).
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and held a post as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpoin (attested 2014).

Nobumasa Miyazaki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2005-2011) and held posts at Toyo University (~2011-2014), Tokyo University of Agriculture (attested 2015), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2015).

Nobumi Iyanaga specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a lecturer post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and a research post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient Tokyo Centre (2008-2014).

Nobunaga Takasa is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held an assistant professor post at the National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 1991) and a researcher post at Rissho University (attested 2001).
